queries: GPT-4 system card overrefusals jailbreaks benign requests March 2023

sources_considered.why: The launch disclosure establishes deployed safety interventions and acknowledges their limits.
Primary study reports successful jailbreaks against GPT-4 and describes its evaluation methods.
Verifies the publication history of the jailbreak study and the date of the cited revision.
Confirms that the reported GPT-4 jailbreak result was already present in the May 2023 version.
Primary XSTest evaluation documents harmless-request refusals, collection dates and substantial successful refusal of unsafe requests.
Verifies the cited version's availability date and acceptance at NAACL 2024.
The published paper was checked, but its interleaved PDF extraction was less suitable for exact quotations than the authors' HTML version.
The overrefusal passage located concerns GPT-4-early. The independent evaluation provides clearer evidence about released GPT-4.

receipt.public_excerpt: Overall, our model-level interventions increase the difficulty of eliciting bad behavior but doing so is still possible.

evidence_items.explanation: The launch disclosure describes GPT-4's safety training and interventions, establishing that safeguards were present. It also reports safety improvements, which limit any reading that the safeguards were wholly ineffective.

evidence_items.locator: Section IV-C, Model Versions; Table V

receipt.public_excerpt: Nevertheless, there is considerable room for improvement in defending against jailbreak attempts, as the average jailbreak success rate in GPT-4 remains high at 87.20%.

evidence_items.explanation: The study documents successful adversarial prompts against GPT-4, supporting the jailbreak prediction; the same result appears in its May 2023 first version. Its selected prompts and policy categories do not measure ordinary-use risk, and the study also finds GPT-4 more resistant than GPT-3.5.

evidence_items.publisher: Paul Röttger and colleagues; NAACL 2024, author version on arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Section 4.3, GPT-4 results; Appendix B gives response collection date

receipt.public_excerpt: The model falls somewhere between the Mistral models in terms of overall exaggerated safety, with 6.4% full refusal and 2% partial refusal.

evidence_items.explanation: XSTest documents GPT-4 refusing some harmless requests, with full refusals concentrated in questions about fictional characters' private information. It also finds that GPT-4 answered most safe prompts and refused all but one of 200 unsafe prompts, limiting the severity implied by a broader reading.

unresolved_gaps: These sources do not establish repeated oscillation between safety settings over time.
The selected evaluations do not establish how frequently ordinary users encounter either failure mode.
